 Main Card Results | UFC Fight Night: Cortes Acosta vs Walker
 Live Results, Highlights, Post-Fight Interviews With The Main Card Winners And More From UFC Fight Night: Cortes Acosta vs Walker, Live From Meta APEX In Las Vegas On November 7 
 By E. Spencer Kyte, On X: @SpencerKyte
 • Nov. 8, 2026
 Following an entertaining preliminary card slate, the action at the Meta APEX shifted to the main card and remained entertaining and eventful.
 Mitch Raposo pushed his winning streak to three by spoiling Marcus Degli’s promotional debut before Nina Milosevic and Lucas Fernando found success in their individual sophomore efforts inside the Octagon. Elijah Smith made a statement with a one-minute knockout of Davey Grant and Tatiana Suarez maintained her place in the title queue with a co-main event win over Virna Jandiroba, setting the stage for Johnny Walker’s wild third-round stoppage win over Waldo Cortes Acosta to wrap up the night.
 If you missed out on any of the action, check out our recaps below in order to get caught up.
 Main Card Results, Highlights & More: 
 More Coverage: Prelim Results | Scorecards 
 Johnny Walker defeated Waldo Cortes Acosta by TKO (strikes) at 2:27 of Round 3 
 Johnny Walker punched his ticket to the Top 10 in the heavyweight division, rallying to knock out Waldo Cortes Acosta in the third round to close things out at the Meta APEX on Saturday night.

 Johnny Walker Stops Cortes Acosta In Round 3 | UFC Fight Night: Cortes Acosta vs Walker
 / 
 Live 
 The Brazilian began the fight by chopping away at Cortes Acosta’s legs, but the Dominican battler refused to check the kicks or take a backwards step, continually pushing forward and pressuring the divisional newcomer. After a second round where it seemed like Cortes Acosta was in complete control, Walker went high with a question mark kick that bounced off the dome of “Salsa Boy” and gave the entertaining Brazilian the opportunity to chase down the finish.
 That’s now consecutive stoppage wins since moving to heavyweight for Walker, who took the fight on short notice and catapulted himself into the thick of the title chase with this victory. He profiled as an intriguing addition to the weight class when he announced the move and has proven it to be true in quick fashion thus far.
 Tatiana Suarez defeated Virna Jandiroba by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) 
 Tatiana Suarez secured her third straight win on Saturday, grinding out a decision victory over fellow recent title challenger Virna Jandiroba to maintain her place in the pecking order in the 115-pound weight class.
 This was a largely uneventful contest, honestly, with Suarez chasing takedowns, Jandiroba initially defending well, and the most exciting moment coming at the close of the second when the Brazilian dove on a kneebar that looked deep but came too late. Suarez spent more than half of the fight working from top position, and while she didn’t do any really significant damage because Jandiroba did a good job of tying her up, the American was clearly the more effective of the two.
 Suarez continues to stand as one of the best in the division, with her lone loss coming in her championship battle with Zhang Weili at the start of last year. Unless the Chinese superstar is going to make her return to the division, a date with current champion Mackenzie Dern could very well be next.
 Elijah Smith defeated Davey Grant by KO (right hand) at 1:00 of Round 1 
 Elijah Smith made a statement on Saturday in the final fight of his contract, sparking Davey Grant in the first round to move to 4-0 inside the Octagon.

 That’s now nine straight wins overall for the Season 8 Dana White’s Contender Series grad, who continues to show he has a bright future in the bantamweight division. This is the kind of win that should carry “Swift” into a marquee matchup next time out.
 Lucas Fernando defeated Billy Elekana by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Lucas Fernando turned in a solid effort in his sophomore appearance on Saturday, halting the three-fight winning streak of Billy Elekana to push his winning streak to five and his record to 15-3 overall.

 The Brazilian took the fight to Elekana from the outset, closing the distance and putting hands on the Las Vegas native from the rip. After stinging him in the first, Fernando continued to land with force throughout the second before Elekana secured a takedown early in the third but failed to do much with it.
 Fernando came out on the favorable side of the scorecards, again resetting the floor for where he stands in the light heavyweight ranks. As he continues to gain more experience and grow more as an athlete, there is clearly room for him to advance in the 205-pound weight class. 
 Nina Milošević defeated Priscila Cachoeira by TKO (strikes) at 3:40 of Round 2 
 Nina Milošević blew through veteran Priscila Cachoeira to secure her second consecutive stoppage win inside the Octagon and take another step forward in the women’s bantamweight division.

 Milošević raced across the canvas and deposited the Brazilian on the deck within the first five seconds, instantly working to her back and attacking with short shots while constantly thinking about a choke, cranking up the intensity in the final minute. Cachoeira survived the first-round onslaught but eventually got put right back into the same position, where Milošević pounded out the finish.

 This was a mauling for the streaking and talented newcomer, who looked outstanding in Belgrade and turned in an impressive follow-up here. She’s still a little green and needs to tighten up a couple things, but Milošević is clearly an interesting addition to the weight class and someone to keep close tabs on going forward.
 Mitch Raposo defeated Marcos Degli by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Mitch Raposo and Marcos Degli opened the main card with a classic flyweight battle, both men having their moments and the action staying swift and steady for all 15 minutes.

 Mitch Raposo Post-Fight Interview | UFC Fight Night: Cortes Acosta vs Walker
 / 
 Live 
 Raposo did well to pressure as much as possible, landing the greater volume throughout against the highly regarded recent Contender Series grad. Degli landed the most noticeable individual shots and opened up Raposo early in the third, but the Massachusetts native just continued to press forward, his pace and volume seemingly giving him the edge in the entertaining three-round affair.
 When the tens and nines were totalled, it was indeed Raposo that came out ahead, pushing his winning streak to three while spoiling Degli’s debut and halting his 13-fight winning streak. This was a great performance from Raposo and arguably the biggest win of his career, putting him in a position to earn another step up next time out.
